name: Gochujang crispy tofu bowls
description: Cornflour-crisped tofu in a sticky gochujang-soy-honey glaze over rice, charred broccoli, sesame.
spice_note: Extra gochugaru or chilli crisp on your bowl only.
tip: Batch the glaze ×3 — it keeps two weeks and upgrades everything.

name: Miso-ginger salmon traybake
description: Salmon fillets in miso-ginger-maple glaze roasted with pak choi and sweet potato wedges.
spice_note: Shichimi togarashi or chilli oil over your fillet.
tip: Salmon is amber-list: 2–3 fish meals a week total is the ceiling.

name: Thai green curry, tofu & green beans
description: Green curry with tofu, green beans, bamboo shoots and Thai basil over jasmine rice — base kept at 🌶🌶.
spice_note: Sliced bird’s-eye chillies and extra paste fried in oil, spooned over your bowl.
tip: Check the paste is shrimp-paste-free (vegetarian ones are) — keeps it firmly green-list.

name: Yakitori-style chicken skewers
description: Chicken thigh skewers glazed with soy-mirin-ginger tare, grilled spring onions, rice, quick-pickled radish.
spice_note: Ichimi/chilli flakes on yours.
tip: One of your two weekly chicken slots.

name: Dan dan-ish noodles (soy mince)
description: Sichuan-style sesame-chilli sauce, crispy soy mince, wheat noodles, wilted greens, crushed peanuts. Sauce built to 🌶🌶.
spice_note: Double chilli oil + extra Sichuan pepper ground over your bowl — proper má là.
tip: Full-flavour flagship. Chilli oil jar = pantry MVP.

name: Vietnamese lemongrass chicken
description: Caramelised lemongrass-chilli chicken with rice, pickled carrot, herbs and nuoc-cham-style dressing (light on fish sauce).
spice_note: Fresh red chilli in your dressing.
tip: Fish sauce stays at teaspoons — flavour without the purine load.

name: Kimchi fried rice + fried egg
description: Day-old rice, kimchi and its juice, spring onion, sesame, topped with a crispy fried egg each.
spice_note: Gochugaru in the pan-half that becomes your portion.
tip: The 15-minute emergency dinner. Cook extra rice earlier in the week on purpose.

name: Salt & pepper crispy tofu
description: Takeaway-style crispy tofu with fried garlic, chilli and spring onion over rice and charred tenderstem.
spice_note: Keep half the fried chillies aside and pile them on yours.

name: Teriyaki white fish, sesame greens
description: Cod or haddock in quick teriyaki, steamed rice, sesame-garlic spring greens.
spice_note: Chilli oil over your fillet.
tip: White fish is the gentlest fish choice for urate.

name: Mapo tofu (mushroom-free)
description: Tofu in a fiery-but-shared doubanjiang and Sichuan pepper sauce with soy mince, over rice. Base at 🌶🌶.
spice_note: Extra doubanjiang fried in chilli oil, spooned over yours — restores full Sichuan violence.
tip: Classically has mushroom or pork — this version needs neither and loses nothing.

name: Singapore noodles, egg & veg
description: Curried rice vermicelli with egg ribbons, peppers, beansprouts and spring onion.
spice_note: Fresh red chilli + hot curry powder pinch on your half.

name: Massaman-style sweet potato & peanut curry
description: Mild-warm coconut curry with sweet potato, peanuts, tofu and rice — the batch-cook king.
spice_note: Crispy chilli oil on top of yours.
tip: Doubles brilliantly — freeze two portions, win a future Tuesday.

name: Bibimbap bowls
description: Rice bowls with seasoned spinach, carrot, courgette, marinated tofu, fried egg and gochujang sauce.
spice_note: Your sauce = gochujang + gochugaru; hers straight gochujang.

name: Miso soba with edamame & greens
description: Chilled or warm soba in miso-sesame dressing with edamame, shredded greens and nori.
spice_note: Rayu (Japanese chilli oil) over yours.
tip: The night-before-long-run dinner: carby, quick, gentle.

name: Sichuan-style aubergine, rice
description: Silky roasted aubergine in garlic-chilli-black-vinegar sauce, rice, sesame. Sauce at 🌶🌶.
spice_note: Dried chillies fried crisp in oil, crumbled over your plate.

name: Ginger & spring onion steamed sea bass
description: Cantonese-style: steamed sea bass, hot oil over ginger and spring onion, soy, rice and greens.
spice_note: Fresh sliced chilli under the hot oil on your fillet.

name: Paneer tikka traybake, flatbreads
description: Yogurt-spiced paneer and peppers roasted hot, with flatbreads, mint yogurt and tomato-onion salad (no cucumber).
spice_note: Kashmiri chilli + green chilli in your half of the marinade.
tip: Dairy protein = actively gout-protective. Full-flavour and cheap.

name: Chana masala + rice
description: Deeply spiced chickpea curry — tomato, ginger, garam masala — with rice or flatbreads.
spice_note: Tadka of green chillies and chilli powder in hot oil, poured over your bowl.
tip: Cheapest meal in the bank. Legume purines are green-list — enjoy freely.

name: Egg & tofu pad thai-style noodles
description: Rice noodles, tamarind-soy-lime sauce, tofu, egg, beansprouts, peanuts, plenty of lime.
spice_note: Dried chilli flakes fried with your portion.
tip: Traditional fish sauce swapped for soy + tamarind — you will not miss it.

name: Tofu & veg laksa
description: Rich coconut-chilli noodle soup with fried tofu, green beans and beansprouts. Broth built to 🌶🌶.
spice_note: Sambal or extra laksa paste fried in oil, stirred into your bowl only.

name: Chipotle black bean chilli
description: Deep smoky chilli — chipotle, cumin, dark chocolate — with black beans, peppers and sweet potato. Lime, yogurt and coriander on top.
tip: The batch-cook champion of the whole bank — makes 4, freezes perfectly. Chilli heat lives in the chipotle, so scale it to taste.

name: Black bean & sweet potato tacos, chipotle slaw
description: Cumin-roasted sweet potato and smoky beans in warm tortillas, with crunchy chipotle-lime cabbage slaw and feta.
tip: Feta as accent, not blanket — keeps it light while adding the salty hit.

name: Baja-style fish tacos
description: Spiced pan-fried white fish, quick-pickled onion, shredded cabbage, lime crema and hot sauce at the table.
tip: Frozen white fish is cheaper and works fine here — one of your 2–3 weekly fish slots.

name: Huevos rancheros
description: Eggs poached in a chilli-tomato sauce over crisped tortillas with black beans, feta and avocado.
tip: Eggs are green-list and cheap. Brilliant post-long-run dinner.

name: Charred corn & bean burrito bowls
description: Coriander-lime rice, black beans, blistered corn, pico de gallo, avocado and a smoky yogurt drizzle.
tip: Assembles from pantry in 25 minutes. The lunchbox version of itself the next day.

name: Chicken tinga tostadas
description: Shredded chicken braised in smoky chipotle-tomato sauce, piled on crisp tortillas with slaw, feta and lime.
tip: One of your two weekly chicken slots.

name: Salsa verde bean enchiladas
description: Tortillas rolled around black beans and peppers, baked under tangy tomatillo-style green salsa and a little melted cheese.
tip: Comfort-food category, big flavour, cheese kept to a modest layer.

name: Peruvian aji verde chicken & potatoes
description: Cumin-roasted chicken and crushed potatoes with a punchy green sauce of chilli, coriander, lime and yogurt.
tip: The aji verde keeps a week and turns leftovers into a different meal.

name: Shakshuka with feta
description: Eggs baked in a spiced pepper-tomato sauce with cumin, paprika and harissa, crumbled feta, flatbread to mop.
tip: 20-minute dinner, all green-list. Add a tin of chickpeas to make it bigger on hungry days.

name: Harissa cauliflower & chickpea traybake
description: Whole roasted cauliflower florets and chickpeas in harissa and cumin, lemon-tahini yogurt, pomegranate and herbs.
tip: One tray, huge flavour, dirt cheap. Cauliflower is high-purine on paper and completely fine in practice.

name: Chickpea, squash & apricot tagine
description: Warm-spiced stew — cinnamon, ginger, ras el hanout — with butternut, chickpeas and dried apricots over couscous. Harissa at the table.
tip: Traditionally has olives — left out entirely, and the apricots carry it. Heat added at the table.

name: Mujadara — lentils, rice & crispy onions
description: Cumin-scented lentils and rice under a mountain of deeply caramelised onions, with herby yogurt and tomato salad.
tip: The cheapest dinner in the file and one of the best. No heat as written — chilli oil at the table if you want it.

name: Berbere lentil stew
description: Ethiopian-spiced red lentils, fiery and fragrant, with collard-style greens and flatbread or rice.
tip: Properly hot as written — the berbere does it. Halve the spice for a milder pan.

name: Baked falafel patties, tahini sauce
description: Herby chickpea patties baked crisp, with lemon-tahini sauce, tomato-red onion salad and warm flatbreads.
tip: Salad is tomato-and-onion rather than the usual cucumber-heavy version.

name: Za’atar salmon with bulgur & herbs
description: Salmon crusted in za’atar over lemony bulgur wheat loaded with parsley, mint, spring onion and pomegranate.
tip: Counts toward your 2–3 weekly fish meals.

name: Turkish red lentil soup, chilli butter
description: Silky red lentil and carrot soup finished with paprika-chilli oil, lemon and torn flatbread.
tip: Pre-long-run dinner or the night you cannot face cooking. Freezes well.

name: Harissa halloumi & chickpea traybake
description: Halloumi, chickpeas, peppers and red onion roasted hard in harissa and honey, with lemon yogurt and couscous.
tip: Halloumi is the flavour accent; the chickpeas carry the protein.

name: Spiced lentil köfte with yogurt & sumac
description: Red lentil and bulgur köfte, pan-crisped, with garlicky yogurt, sumac onions and a tomato-herb salad.
tip: Comfort food that happens to be almost entirely legumes and grains.

name: Sesame-soy tofu rice bowl
description: Ready-marinated tofu, pouch rice, edamame and carrot ribbons under a soy-sesame drizzle. Boxed cold, eaten cold or warm.
spice_note: Chilli crisp spooned over just before you eat.
tip: Frozen edamame defrosts in the box by lunchtime — no pan, no kettle.

name: Kimchi, egg & nori rice box
description: Cold rice, kimchi, two boiled eggs, gochujang mayo and torn nori. Four minutes if the eggs are already done.
spice_note: Extra gochugaru through the mayo.
tip: Boil six eggs on Sunday and this becomes the fastest box in the file.

name: Vermicelli, herb & pickled carrot pot
description: Kettle-soaked rice noodles, smoked tofu, shredded lettuce, masses of mint and coriander, nuoc-cham-style dressing in a separate pot.
spice_note: Sliced red chilli in the dressing jar.
tip: Vermicelli only needs boiling water and three minutes — no hob involved.

name: Tuna-mayo & avocado nori wrap
description: Onigirazu — a nori-wrapped rice sandwich of tuna mayo, avocado and carrot. Cuts in half and holds together in a bag.
spice_note: Wasabi or chilli oil stirred through the mayo.
tip: Tuna is amber-list — keep this to once a week alongside your two fish dinners.

name: Peanut-lime crunch slaw, smoked tofu
description: Cabbage, carrot and pepper shredded fine, smoked tofu battons, peanut-lime-ginger dressing, crushed peanuts on top.
spice_note: Chilli oil or sriracha whisked into the dressing.
tip: Shred a big tub of slaw on Sunday and dress the portion, not the tub — it stays crisp all week.

name: Black bean, feta & avocado wrap
description: Crushed black beans with chipotle and lime, avocado, feta, tomato and red onion rolled tight.
spice_note: Hot sauce straight into the bean mash.
tip: Crush half the beans — that is what stops the wrap unravelling in your bag.

name: Chipotle chickpea & sweetcorn bowl
description: Chickpeas, sweetcorn, pepper and red onion over pouch rice, chipotle-yogurt drizzle, lime and coriander.
spice_note: Extra chipotle paste on your side of the bowl.
tip: Chickpeas and yogurt in one bowl: plant protein plus the dairy that actively lowers urate.

name: Hot-smoked salmon & lime slaw tacos
description: Flaked hot-smoked salmon, sharp lime cabbage slaw, chipotle yogurt and pickled red onion in soft tortillas.
spice_note: Hot sauce over the flaked salmon.
tip: Amber-list — count it as one of your 2–3 weekly fish servings, not an extra.

name: Hummus & za’atar chickpea plate
description: Hummus spread thick, chickpeas tumbled over with za’atar and lemon, tomato-onion-parsley salad, flatbread to scoop.
spice_note: Harissa or chilli flakes swirled through the hummus.
tip: The six-minute lunch. Buy hummus in the big tub — it works out half the price.

name: Herby bulgur, feta & pomegranate jar
description: Tabbouleh-leaning jar: kettle-soaked fine bulgur, a forest of parsley and mint, tomato, spring onion, feta, pomegranate, sumac and lemon.
spice_note: Chilli flakes and extra sumac on top.
tip: Pour boiling water on the bulgur before your shower; it is done before you are.

name: Lentil, beetroot & feta box
description: Ready-cooked puy lentils, vac-packed beetroot, spinach, feta and walnuts under a lemon-tahini dressing.
spice_note: Harissa stirred into the tahini dressing.
tip: Plant purines, dairy protein, deep-pigment veg — about as urate-friendly as a lunch gets.

name: Falafel, tahini & pickled cabbage wrap
description: Shop-bought falafel crumbled into a flatbread with quick vinegar cabbage, tomato, tahini sauce and harissa.
spice_note: Extra harissa striped down the wrap.
tip: Ten minutes of cabbage in vinegar does the job of a proper pickle.

name: Shawarma-spiced chicken & yogurt wrap
description: Cold cooked chicken tossed in baharat and lemon, garlicky yogurt, tomato and onion, rolled in a flatbread.
spice_note: Harissa or chilli sauce through the yogurt.
tip: Uses one of your two weekly chicken slots — cheapest built from Sunday leftovers.

name: Egg mayo & cress sandwich
description: Proper egg mayo — coarsely crushed, mustard-sharp, plenty of black pepper — with cress on thick bread.
spice_note: Sriracha or chilli flakes through the mayo.
tip: Boil a batch of eggs on Sunday and three of these lunches build themselves.

name: Hummus, roast pepper & feta sandwich
description: Jarred roasted peppers, thick hummus, crumbled feta and spinach in seeded bread. No chopping worth the name.
spice_note: Harissa or chilli flakes over the hummus.
tip: A jar of roasted peppers is the single best-value sandwich upgrade in the shop.

name: Cheddar, pickle & apple sandwich
description: Mature cheddar, sweet pickle or chutney, thin apple slices for crunch. The whole thing takes four minutes.
spice_note: Add sliced pickled jalapeño.
tip: Cheese is a gout ally, not a risk — dairy protein actively lowers urate.

name: Tuna crunch & sweetcorn wrap
description: Tuna mixed with sweetcorn, spring onion and half-yogurt mayo, rolled in a tortilla with lettuce.
spice_note: Sriracha stirred into the mix.
tip: Amber-list — one tinned-fish lunch a week, not three.

name: Smashed chickpea & lemon sandwich
description: Chickpeas crushed with yogurt, lemon and mustard into something between houmous and egg mayo. Cheap and genuinely filling.
spice_note: Chilli flakes and a spoon of harissa.
tip: About 45p a sandwich and 15 g of protein. Hard to beat.

name: Chopped chickpea, feta & sweetcorn salad
description: Everything diced to the same size, dressed with lemon and mustard. Travels better than leaves and does not wilt.
spice_note: Chilli flakes over the top.

name: New potato, egg & green bean salad
description: Cold new potatoes, halved boiled eggs, green beans and a mustard-yogurt dressing. Built entirely from things already cooked.
spice_note: Chilli flakes and extra mustard.
tip: Boil extra potatoes with any dinner — this is what they are for.

name: Apple, walnut & cheddar spinach salad
description: Spinach, sharp apple, cubed cheddar and walnuts under a lemon-mustard dressing. Five ingredients, five minutes.
spice_note: Chilli flakes or a spoon of chutney in the dressing.
tip: Add a slice of bread if it is a long-run day — on its own it is light on carbs.

name: Butter bean, roasted pepper & feta salad
description: Tinned butter beans, jarred peppers, feta, red onion and lemon. Almost entirely store-cupboard.
spice_note: Chilli flakes and a spoon of harissa.
tip: Butter beans are the creamiest tinned pulse and criminally underused.

name: Smashed avocado & egg on sourdough
description: Avocado crushed with lemon and salt, halved boiled eggs, chilli flakes and plenty of pepper.
spice_note: More chilli flakes, or chilli oil over the top.

name: Herby white beans on toast
description: Cannellini beans warmed with garlic, lemon and parsley, piled on toast. Ready before the toaster pops twice.
spice_note: Chilli flakes fried into the oil first.
tip: Microwave the beans for 60 seconds if you would rather not touch a pan.

name: Peanut butter, banana & cinnamon toast
description: The three-minute post-long-run lunch: thick peanut butter, sliced banana, cinnamon, a scatter of seeds.
spice_note: Not really a chilli dish. Leave this one alone.
tip: Carbs plus protein within the hour after a long run — pair with skyr for the full 30 g.

name: Cherry, chia & skyr overnight oats
description: The 6 am run-day default: oats soaked overnight in skyr and milk with frozen cherries and chia. Zero effort at the point of eating.
spice_note: Not a chilli dish — a scrape of ginger or cardamom instead.
tip: Dairy protein plus cherries in one bowl — the single most urate-protective breakfast you can eat. Make three jars at once.

name: Skyr, berry & granola bowl
description: Skyr, frozen berries thawed overnight, granola and seeds. Three minutes, 25 g of protein, no cooking.
spice_note: Leave it be.
tip: Skip the honey drizzle — fructose raises urate, and the fruit is doing that job already.

name: Peanut butter & banana porridge
description: Milk-cooked porridge with peanut butter stirred through and banana on top. The pre-long-run breakfast — carbs plus enough fat to keep you going.
spice_note: A pinch of salt does more for this than chilli would.
tip: Eat 90 minutes before a long run. Milk rather than water adds 12 g of protective dairy protein.

name: Scrambled eggs, avocado & toast
description: Soft scrambled eggs, crushed avocado, seeded toast, chilli flakes. The rest-day breakfast that holds until lunch.
spice_note: Chilli flakes or chilli oil over the eggs.
tip: Low and slow off the heat is the whole technique — eggs finish cooking in the pan after you stop.

name: Cherry, banana & skyr recovery smoothie
description: Blitzed straight after a long run: frozen cherries, banana, skyr, milk and oats. Around 30 g of protein and fast carbs in one glass.
spice_note: A knob of ginger blitzed in is the only heat this wants.
tip: Drink within the hour after hard sessions. Tart cherry has the best evidence of any food for both urate and muscle soreness.

name: Miso, egg & nori rice bowl
description: Japanese-style savoury breakfast: hot rice, a soft egg, miso stirred into the grains, nori and spring onion.
spice_note: Chilli oil or shichimi over the egg.
tip: The savoury option for mornings when you cannot face another sweet bowl.

name: Egg, cream cheese & tomato bagel
description: Toasted bagel, cream cheese, sliced boiled egg and tomato. The big-carb morning — race day, long-run day, or any day you woke up hungry.
spice_note: Chilli flakes or hot sauce on the egg.
tip: Practise this one before race day — bagels sit well in a stomach that has to run afterwards.

name: Oat, cherry & seed flapjacks
description: Dense oat flapjacks with dried cherries and seeds. Run fuel, mid-afternoon fuel, or a pocket bar for hill reps.
spice_note: A pinch of chilli in the mix is a real thing, but start with ginger instead.
tip: Cherries are the one food with real evidence behind it for urate — worth building into a weekly bake.

name: Banana, walnut & yogurt loaf
description: Yogurt keeps it damp for four days. Barely sweet, heavy with banana and walnuts — closer to a fuel loaf than a cake.
spice_note: Ginger and cardamom rather than heat.
tip: Freezes in slices — take one out at 6 am and it has thawed by the time you finish a long run.

name: Feta & spinach frittata muffins
description: Baked egg muffins with spinach, feta, spring onion and roasted pepper. Two of these plus fruit is a real lunch.
spice_note: Chilli flakes through the egg mix.
tip: About 9 g of protein each and they keep four days in the fridge. The best lunchbox item in this file.

name: Cheese, carrot & seed savoury muffins
description: Wholemeal savoury muffins with grated carrot, cheddar and seeds. Bread substitute, soup companion, desk snack.
spice_note: Chilli flakes or a spoon of harissa in the batter.
tip: No yeast extract anywhere near these — that stays firmly on the red list.

name: Date, cocoa & peanut energy balls
description: No baking at all: blitz, roll, chill. Dense, chocolatey, and about 90 calories of very portable carbohydrate each.
spice_note: A pinch of chilli with the cocoa actually works here.
tip: Fructose caution: dates are concentrated sugar, so treat these as run fuel rather than all-day grazing.

name: Rice, sesame & maple race bars
description: Sticky pressed rice bars in the Japanese onigiri-meets-flapjack tradition. Easy to chew cold, and survives a pocket.
spice_note: A shake of shichimi if you want a savoury version.
tip: Gut-training food. Start practising these on long runs in Phase 2, not in January.

name: Yogurt & seed soda bread
description: No kneading, no proving, no yeast. Mix, shape, bake — a loaf inside an hour that carries every sandwich above.
spice_note: Not applicable, but chilli-cheese variations exist.
tip: Cheaper than shop sourdough by a distance, and you know exactly what is in it.
